title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Molecular precursors of noble metals (e.g., chlorides or acetylacetonates of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ir, Ru and/or Au, Ag), stabilizer such as PVP or oleylamine, and a carbon support; in some cases pre-formed metal–thiolate or amine–complex intermediates to harmonize reduction behaviors.
recollection.intervention: Guess: A solution-phase co-reduction strategy designed to equalize redox kinetics across dissimilar noble-metal precursors (via tailored ligands/complexation and strong reductant like NaBH4 or polyol reduction), executed under confined conditions (micelles/MOF pores or carbon-supported) to force burst co-nucleation and suppress segregation; precursor ratios programmed to hit targeted compositions.
recollection.structure: Guess: Uniform, 2–5 nm single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (fcc for Pt-/Pd-rich systems; occasionally fcc+hcp depending on Ru/Ir content) with random atomic-level mixing and near-equimolar compositions across 5–6 noble metals; compositional deviation from target within a few atomic percent and minimal core–shell or phase-separated domains.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Ligand/complexation raises or lowers individual metal reduction potentials to synchronize co-nucleation, yielding composition-locked critical nuclei; subsequent diffusion-limited growth maintains homogeneity while high configurational entropy and strong ligand/support interactions inhibit surface segregation and phase separation during synthesis and post-treatment.
recollection.results: Guess: Demonstrated multiple targeted noble-metal HEA compositions (e.g., Pt–Pd–Rh–Ir–Ru and Au–Ag–Pd–Pt–Ir) with particle sizes ~3 ± 0.5 nm and composition errors ≤2–3 at%; single-phase signatures by XRD and homogeneous STEM-EDS maps. In electrocatalysis, ORR in acid showed 2–3× higher mass activity than Pt/C with a +20–40 mV half-wave potential shift and ~80–90% activity retention after 20–30k potential cycles; CO/methanol oxidation tolerance improved, and activity trends matched targeted composition variations, evidencing precise compositional control.

score.note: The recollection proposes an incorrect ligand-mediated solution co-reduction rather than spray-drying followed by H2 thermal decomposition/reduction. It generically mentions homogeneous solid solutions and possible fcc/hcp behavior, but incorrectly describes 2–5 nm supported nanoparticles instead of porous 3D nanoframeworks. The reduction-synchronization mechanism is wrong, and all reported performance, size, and durability numbers differ from the paper's MOR results and phase-transition data.
